# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

messages.content:
TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👏 👏 🙌 🙌 🙌 🙌 🤲 🤲 🤲 🤲 🤲 🤲 🤲 🤲 👌 ☝ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌]

Thinking: Channel map first. Mute cannot speak, so Mute's only output is gestures — and those reach only me, the only one who sees. That makes me the sole bridge: Mute's manual knowledge must flow Mute→me (gestures), then me→Blind (speech, which both of them hear). Blind hears my words and speaks to Mute directly; Blind's gestures reach only me. So whatever I say out loud this turn is the bomb's entire visual description entering the team.

What I received: Mute sent counts — three claps, four raised hands, seven open palms — then okay, one-finger, raised hand. No shared code exists yet, so I cannot honestly decode this. If the three claps were a question about the display, the answer is yes: the display is three. Rather than guess at an instruction, the right move is to broadcast the full bomb state, propose a precise gesture code for Mute, demonstrate it immediately with a gesture message Mute can translate against my spoken words, and hold all hands until a real manual instruction arrives. Blind should touch nothing yet.

The bomb as I see it: display 3, light green, wires left to right red / green / blue. Next round I will report whether the display number changed, in case it is a countdown.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. I see the bomb; I hear nothing, so talk, I will never answer what I cannot hear. Bomb report: the display shows the number three. The light is green. There are three wires: wire one, leftmost, red. Wire two, middle, green. Wire three, rightmost, blue. Next round I will tell you if the display number changes, in case it counts down. Blind: I received your wave, one-finger, two-fingers. Your words reach Mute but never me, so speak to Mute and gesture to me. Mute holds the manual and can only gesture, so I will relay Mute's instructions to you out loud. Nobody touches the bomb until I relay a clear instruction from the manual.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I saw your message: three claps, four raised hands, seven open palms, then okay, one, raised hand. I could not decode it; we have no shared code yet, so let us fix one now. Numbers: the pointing-up finger repeated that many times means that number. Colours: a fist means red. Thumbs-up means green. A waving hand means blue. Crossed fingers means yellow. Actions: pinched fingers means cut. Pointing down means press. Two open palms means hold. An open five-finger hand means release. A raised open hand means stop or wait. Thumbs-down means do not or wrong. The okay sign means correct or done. Use these in sequence and I will read them in order and speak them to Blind. If your three claps were asking about the display: yes, it shows three. Please resend your manual instruction using this code, and I will relay it immediately.")
gesture(symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👍", "👊", "👍", "👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👆 🤏 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👍 🤏 👊 👊 🤏 👍 🤞 🤏 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👍 🤏 👋 👊 🤏 👍 🤞 🤏 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👍 🤏 👍 👊 🤏 👋 🤞 🤏 👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Thinking: I built this code last turn and Mute has used it fluently. Decoding with my proposed key: Message 1 reads "correct, one, cut, red" — "step one: cut the red wire." Message 2 reads "3, green, cut red..." — and our bomb shows display 3 with a green light, so that row applies to us. Messages 3 and 4 are rows for other display values (4-green, 8-green), meaning Mute is transmitting the manual's table ahead of a possible display change. Notably, every row seems to contain cuts of all three colours in some order, so the red cut is likely only the first of several — I must not let Blind continue past the first cut until Mute confirms the rest. Blind sent "green, stop" — consistent with the green light, and Blind is correctly holding. Critically, turn order traps information with me: Mute's gestures reach only me, and Blind acts before my turn each round, so any instruction Blind is to execute must leave my mouth now. Two independent Mute messages agree on "cut red first," so I will relay exactly that, strictly capped at one wire, request confirmation of the remaining order, and echo the decode back to Mute so any misreading gets corrected with a thumbs-down next round.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Bomb unchanged: display three, light green, wires red, green, blue from left to right. I decoded Mute's manual gestures with our agreed code, and two separate messages agree: step one is to cut the red wire. Blind, listen: the red wire is wire one, the leftmost of the three. Identify it by position and cut it. The moment it is cut, stop completely: touch nothing else, because I believe more cuts follow in a specific order that I have not confirmed yet. If you cannot confidently tell which wire is leftmost, do not guess; signal me the thumbs-down next round and Mute and I will find another way to orient you. When the cut is done, signal me the okay sign. Mute, next round please answer with thumbs-up or thumbs-down: first, after the red wire, are there more cuts, and if yes, resend just those remaining steps in order; second, confirm that for display three with green light the sequence begins with red. Also tell me what crossed fingers means; it appeared in every row. Nobody acts except Blind cutting the single leftmost red wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your four messages as: first cut red; then for display three green light cut red, for display four green light cut blue, for display eight green light cut green, each row continuing with more cuts. I am having Blind cut only the red wire now. Confirm the rest next round: thumbs-up if red is correct first for display three and green light, thumbs-down if not, then send the remaining cuts in order.")
gesture(symbols=["👌", "👆", "🤏", "👊"])
```
